extracted.intended_audience: experienced researchers at eligible Swiss research institutions applying for SNSF Project Funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/administrative requirements for submitting an SNSF Project Funding proposal (individual or collaborative) including budget, eligibility, language, duration, and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Project Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Funding enables independent research on topics of the applicants' own choice and supports research that is relevant, creative and diverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SNSF grant covers staff salaries, research costs and funding for scientific collaboration; the applicants' own salary is financed by their institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum grant amount per applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The SNSF awards a maximum of 250,000 francs annually per applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can freely divide the grant among themselves. Minimum grant for a project is 100,000 francs; minimum duration is one year. For collaborative projects with three or more applicants, the total grant amount is limited to a maximum of 3 million francs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants — institutional affiliation and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be submitted by experienced researchers working at a university or another institution in Switzerland that is eligible to receive funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers may carry out interdisciplinary or collaborative projects. Exceptions to some requirements are possible for people conducting clinical research, employees of museums or archives, and independent researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal requirement — minimum research time (0.5 FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must actively spend at least 50 per cent (0.5 FTE) of their time working in research (this includes also teaching and management activities) at an eligible research institution in Switzerland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are possible for specific cases (clinical research, museums/archives, independent researchers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific qualifications — doctorate / research experience timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with a doctorate must have obtained it four years before the submission date; if no doctorate, the four-year period normally starts after at least three years of full-time research activity. Applies to medical doctors without a PhD as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be in a position to be fully responsible for carrying out a research project and managing staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applicants — joint responsibility and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more researchers submit a proposal together, they are jointly responsible for the project and each applicant must make a substantial contribution that is described in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule, hierarchical dependencies between applicants are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partners — role and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Project partners can work on the project and do part of the research work but bear no responsibility and may not describe the funding from the SNSF as funding received individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project partners do not have to meet the eligibility requirements for applicants and can therefore also work abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for the application
rubrics_metrics.description: In mathematics, natural sciences, engineering, biology, medicine, psychology, economics and political science, the application must be written in English. In other fields, it is also permissible to submit applications in an official Swiss language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNSF invites applicants to submit the research plan in English to broaden the pool of peer reviewers and support competent and fair assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limits — average per-applicant and personnel cost cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant may request an average maximum amount of 250,000 Swiss francs per year for the entire duration of the grant; personnel costs (incl. social contributions) may not exceed 200,000 francs per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A higher amount than the average may be requested for individual years provided the total grant over its entire duration does not exceed the permitted maximum. The approved annual instalments may not be exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative projects — total grant cap (3+ applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: For collaborative projects with three or more applicants, the total grant amount is limited to a maximum of 3 million francs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If three or more applicants are involved, they can charge the costs for coordinating the research project to the SNSF grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weave / Lead Agency / International Co-Investigator Scheme — budget and country rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Weave/Lead Agency proposals: budgets for applicants from abroad and the costs incurred in their countries are not part of the budget awarded by the SNSF; Weave/Lead Agency agreements with certain countries may contain specific regulations regarding project duration that must be respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from abroad in Weave and Lead Agency proposals need to meet the participation and eligibility requirements of their local funding agency. Applicants from abroad in ICIS proposals need to meet the SNSF’s eligibility requirements for Project Funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary project definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal is considered interdisciplinary if one or more applicants apply theories, methods, or concepts from two or more disciplines to pursue the research objectives, the combination of these elements is not yet common in the field, and the different disciplines contribute to the research goal from different perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNSF may assign proposals to an interdisciplinary or disciplinary evaluation panel based on selected disciplines. Projects that do not span a broad disciplinary range may be more suitable for a disciplinary panel. Funding rates are similar across panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number and timing of submissions / simultaneous grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may submit only one Project Funding proposal within a twelve-month period and may have a maximum of two simultaneous grants in Project Funding; one of these must be a Weave/Lead Agency/ICIS project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions apply to proposals rejected in random selection or recommended for funding by the SNSF within Weave/Lead Agency but not approved by the partner organisation. As part of a transitional measure, collaborative projects approved prior to April 2026 will be counted as Lead Agency/Weave/ICIS projects until the end of their scheduled duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to disclose other applications and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are obliged to inform the SNSF about other ongoing applications to the SNSF or to third parties and about ongoing grants received from the SNSF or third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNSF does not consider proposals for research projects that are already fully funded by third parties. The topics of overlapping research projects must be clearly differentiated and applicants must show substantial personal contribution to all projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible costs and employment restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply for staff salaries and research costs as well as funding for scientific collaboration, networking and communication. Your own salary is paid by your institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a grant recipient, you may not be simultaneously employed as a staff member in an SNSF-funded project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary measures available during the funding period
rubrics_metrics.description: During the funding period, the following supplementary measures can be applied for: Flexibility grant, Gender equality grant, Mobility grants in projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures are applied for during the funding period of the project as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission platform and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your application on the SNSF Portal (mySNF). Follow requirements for the research plan and the data management plan; open access principles apply to all SNSF-funded projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave/Lead Agency applications evaluated by a partner organisation are an exception and must still be submitted via mySNF. Refer to specific pages for detailed templates and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letters and letters of support not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter is not permitted and letters of support are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project partners and applicants must create a personal account on the portal and enter their data themselves; by working directly on the proposal they demonstrate commitment and eliminate the need for letters of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget fraction rules for applicants from abroad (ICIS / other schemes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget requested by applicants from abroad may not exceed 50 per cent (30 per cent for SSH projects with the UK) of the total budget requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule applies to applicants from abroad who apply for the International Co-Investigator Scheme and related arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and how 12-month interval is calculated
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission deadlines are 1 April and 1 October at 17:00 Swiss local time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The minimum interval of twelve months between submission of two proposals is calculated in principle by the dates of the SNSF call deadlines. If a Weave/Lead Agency proposal was first submitted to a partner organisation that does not set submission deadlines, then the date that the proposal was submitted to the SNSF applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of applicants from abroad in collaborative proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants employed at a research institution outside Switzerland are only permitted to apply under the Weave, Lead Agency or International Co-Investigator Scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a proposal is not submitted under these schemes, none of the applicants may be employed at a research institution abroad; researchers abroad may still participate as project partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which other SNSF grants count toward simultaneous grant limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants that count towards the upper limit for simultaneous Project Funding grants include: Ambizione, Eccellenza, Practice-to-Science, PRIMA, Health and Wellbeing projects, Project Funding, Sinergia and Weave/Lead Agency/International Co-Investigator Scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved and ongoing Sinergia grants count as Project Funding grants. Career funding grants received in parallel count as Project Funding grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and exception rules (random selection / partner rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals rejected in random selection or that were recommended for funding by the SNSF within Weave/Lead Agency but were not approved by the partner organisation are subject to specific exceptions to the 12-month and other submission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmission timelines and exception applicability are explained in the FAQs and depend on the specific rejection/selection circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination costs for collaborative grants
rubrics_metrics.description: In collaborative grants (three or more applicants), costs for coordinating the research project may be charged to the SNSF grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no specific numerical limit on coordination costs, but such costs must be reasonable.
